title: Basic-auth password policy must be enforced in the store's update_user as well as create_user
answers: basic auth password can be set shorter than the minimum length on update
admin or user changes password to a too-short value and it is accepted
where is the basic-auth password length policy enforced
password reset bypasses the 12 character minimum
body:
Invariant: every password write goes through the length policy in mlflow/utils/validation.py:_validate_password (minimum 12 characters), before hashing.
Enforced by: SqlAlchemyStore.update_user in mlflow/server/auth/sqlalchemy_store.py calls _validate_password inside its `if password is not None:` block, and create_user calls it too.
What breaks if skipped: update_user and update_user_password accepted passwords shorter than the policy, while create_user rejected them. Validation must run before generate_password_hash, so a rejected update leaves the stored hash unchanged.
Constraints: update_user is the store-level choke point for REST, signup, bootstrap and admin password changes, so do not add the check only in a REST handler. Updates with password None (for example is_admin only) must not be validated. Keep the error code INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE.
applies: Any new code path that creates or changes a basic-auth user's password in the auth store.
says: Users can change their password to something shorter than the twelve character minimum length requirement.
Admin password updates accept short passwords that violate our twelve character minimum length rule.
Enforce the twelve character minimum password length when editing existing user accounts.
The password reset screen allows saving passwords that are under twelve characters long.
Updating an existing login password bypasses the length restrictions enforced during initial registration.
search: Every basic-auth password write must validate the minimum 12-character length policy in mlflow/utils/validation.py:_validate_password before hashing, enforced in SqlAlchemyStore.update_user as well as create_user in mlflow/server/auth/sqlalchemy_store.py. Applies to any new code path creating or changing a basic-auth user's password in the auth store, ensuring rejected updates leave stored hashes unchanged. Because update_user is the store choke point for REST, signup, bootstrap, and admin changes, do not place the check only in REST handlers, do not validate updates where password is None, and keep error code INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE.
